newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin fines IPB fund CZK 10 mln.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin fines IPB fund CZK 10 mln.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry on Thursday said it had fined investment fund manager Prvni Investicni a.s.(PIAS), a unit of bank IPB, the maximum allowed fine of 10 million crowns for illegal financing operations and other violations.

The ministry added in a statement that it had also ordered changes in the management of PIAS, and said it must change "its depositors for its unit trusts and investment funds", which is currently IPB.
It also must cancel its contract making IPB its broker.
"Violations of the law on investment companies and investment funds were found on the basis of a probe in investment funds and unit trusts managed (by PIAS)," a ministry statement said.

"(This) concerns mainly violations of the rules of securities trading, performing operations having the character of forbidden credit extension and failing to adhere to the legal limits of holding of securities which are not publicly tradable," it added.
PIAS is the largest Czech investment fund manager, controlling holdings of some 30 billion crowns.
The statement did not elaborate on the violations. Officials at PIAS were not immediately available for comment.
IPB, the Czech Republic's third largest bank, is in the process of being privatised by the government, which is looking to sell its 36 percent stake in the bank to Japan's Nomura International.
Finance Minister Ivan Pilip has said that a closing of the probe into PIAS's operations was necessary before the the privatisation could finish.
Nomura already controls a five percent stake in IPB through the Czech-registered firm Nutshell s.r.o..

The privatisation process of IPB has already hit a bump when police arrested the bank's general director Jiri Tesar and his deputy for alleged fraud. The two have since been released from jail, but an investigation into the case continues.
Finance Ministry officials and Tesar, who stepped down as director at IPB's annual general meeting in June, said the the privatisation process should be finalised by the end of summer.
